clue.text: Teacher's role, to sound disapproving as start of religious service missed

parts.note: tut is the clicking noise of disapproval

indicators.note: points at the opening letter of the service word as the one to go
something missed is left out, so a letter is dropped here

parts.note: worship is a church service

explanation.surface: A teaching job turns sour when the tutor tuts at people who skip the start of chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorship is the post or office held by a private teacher, so it is that teacher's role.

clue.text: Having little time, Hammerstein fails to finish musical work

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the lyricist's first name loses its final letter

parts.note: Oscar Hammerstein, the Broadway lyricist

explanation.surface: A rushed Broadway lyricist leaves his latest show unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammerstein's first name was Oscar; cut its last letter to get OSCA after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera, an example of a musical work.

clue.text: Gnome doesn't exist? It's impossible to know

definitions.meaning: a gnome is a pithy maxim, so no such maxim is to be had
an idiom meaning nobody can tell what will happen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' is not the garden figure but an old word for an aphorism or saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means one cannot predict the outcome; read literally it says no saying exists.

clue.text: Girl ain't badly-behaved creature

indicators.note: unruly letters that misbehave end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A naughty girl is compared to some wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly-behaved' rearranges GIRL AINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtail is an animal with a banded tail, such as a ringtail possum or cacomistle.

clue.text: Miles away, an art museum — and its contents?

indicators.note: the miles letter is sent off, removed from the museum name

parts.note: the Hermitage in St Petersburg is a famous art museum

explanation.surface: A gallery far off, with its treasures inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes M (miles) from HERMITAGE; the definition plays on a museum holding a nation's inherited treasures.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum's contents are a nation's inherited treasures, its cultural legacy from the past.

clue.text: A sheep has fallen into river, it's plain to see

indicators.note: the sheep tumbles into the river, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep tumbles into a river, a scene easy to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like 'obvious' in 'plain to see', but it is the noun: a high Andean plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramo is a high treeless plateau in the tropical Andes, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Half-heartedly look after group in maths class

indicators.note: only half of the doubled central pair survives, so one middle letter goes

parts.note: to cosset is to pamper or care for

explanation.surface: A teacher looks after a group of pupils without much enthusiasm in a maths lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: COSSET has a doubled S at its heart; 'Half-heartedly' keeps only one.
explanation.definitionFit: In group theory a coset is a class formed by multiplying a subgroup by one element.

clue.text: Party food is served up out of saucepan actually

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read from bottom to top
the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Party nibbles really are dished out of a saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes EPANAC from saucEPAN ACtually; 'served up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A canape is a small savoury snack served at drinks parties.

clue.text: Behaved aggressively, as dentist's patient might have done?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for acting in a hostile, threatening way

definitions.text: as dentist's patient might have done?
definitions.meaning: literally, a patient opens wide and bares the teeth for inspection

explanation.definitionFit: Baring one's teeth is a snarling threat, hence acting aggressively, and literally what a dental patient does.

clue.text: Presenters using sensitive language mostly

parts.note: tender means sore or sensitive

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Erse is Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Broadcasters who choose their words carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is Gaelic; 'mostly' trims it to ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderers are people who present or offer something, such as bids or payment.

clue.text: I resent revolutionary educationist

indicators.note: turning over the letters, revolting against their order

explanation.surface: A rebel declares resentment of a schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges I RESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Steiner founded the Waldorf school movement, so he is a noted educationist.

clue.text: Smuggled dope in port once

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them
a goon is a dope, a fool

explanation.surface: Drugs were smuggled into a harbour long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' is not drugs but a fool, GOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon is the former name of Yangon, Myanmar's main seaport.

clue.text: Salesman's deep-red colour, appearing unclothed?

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, so first and last letters go

parts.note: magenta is a purplish-red colour

explanation.surface: A salesman in crimson looks oddly naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unclothed' strips the first and last letters off MAGENTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales agent is a representative who sells on behalf of a firm.

clue.text: US magazine article that sounds the alarm?

parts.note: Time is the American news weekly
a piece is an article in a newspaper

explanation.surface: An American news story that raises the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a definition with the magazine but supplies PIECE; the clock is the thing with an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm clock is one kind of clock, which rings to wake the sleeper.

clue.text: English town is in possession of items from Ireland?

parts.note: has means owns
things, said with a stereotypical Irish accent dropping the h

explanation.surface: A town that holds goods brought from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish accent joke turns 'things' into 'tings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is a town on the East Sussex coast, site of the 1066 battle.

clue.text: Panel wanted to take charge of decision-making body

parts.note: to head is to lead
a board of directors makes decisions

explanation.surface: A committee member wants to chair the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A headboard is the upright panel at the head of a bed.

clue.text: Precious English book reviewed

indicators.note: looked at again, read back the other way

parts.note: vol is short for volume

explanation.surface: A treasured English book gets a critical write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns E VOL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious and love are both affectionate terms of address, as in 'my precious'.

clue.text: Sea captain, without hesitation, would hoist sail on this

parts.note: the main is the open sea

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: a master commands a merchant ship
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A sea captain, quick to act, would raise sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainmast is the principal mast, on which the mainsail is raised.

clue.text: One organising publicity for car on the radio

indicators.note: heard over the air, sounding like the words

parts.note: for is pro, car is motor

explanation.surface: A publicist advertising a car on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter organises and publicises events or products.

clue.text: Declare river has changed direction in the end

indicators.text: has changed direction in the end
indicators.note: the last letter, a compass point, becomes another compass point

parts.note: the Avon flows through Stratford

explanation.surface: Someone states that a river finally changed course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has changed direction in the end' swaps the final N (north) of AVON for W (west).
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or state openly.

clue.text: It's just the fine, dry state of the weather

definitions.meaning: the quality of being just, equity

definitions.text: the fine, dry state of the weather
definitions.meaning: fair weather is fine and dry

explanation.definitionFit: Fairness means justice, and also fine conditions when the weather is fair.

clue.text: Line written up in verse

indicators.note: in a down clue, read upwards

parts.note: an axis is a reference line

explanation.surface: A line composed in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' reverses AXIS to SIXA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixain is a stanza of six lines of verse.

clue.text: As tonic, take tablet if laid up

indicators.note: in a down clue, both pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: to pill is to dose with a tablet

explanation.surface: Taking a pill as a pick-me-up when bedridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' reverses PILL IF as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that acts as a tonic.

clue.text: Britain takes a large number, reportedly, from South American country

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase is matched by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: BR for Britain, then A and zillion, a huge number

explanation.surface: Britain receives many immigrants from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazilian is the adjective for something from Brazil.

clue.text: In pool, time for some rhythm

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the pool word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Swimmers keep a steady beat in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the measured pattern of rhythm in verse.

clue.text: Mopes around in town

indicators.note: the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone sulks about town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges MOPES; EPSOM is a Surrey town famous for the Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a town in Surrey, home of the Derby racecourse.

clue.text: Woman's a great pain

parts.note: big means great
an ail is an ailment or trouble

explanation.surface: Some woman is a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a woman's name, and also an old word for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Performer about to make comeback introducing extract from Hair

indicators.note: returning, so read backwards

parts.note: ca is circa, about
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A performer returns to the stage with a song from the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make comeback' reverses CA to AC.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer on stage or screen.

clue.text: Like getting home to eat heartily

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
in means at home

explanation.surface: Happy to be home for a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dig in is an idiom for starting to eat with gusto.

clue.text: Mahler's pieces (not the Fourth) on favourite tape

indicators.note: placed after the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged
leave out the fourth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Selections from Mahler, skipping his Fourth Symphony, recorded on a favourite tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the Fourth' drops L, the fourth letter of MAHLERS (the possessive S counts); 'pieces' rearranges what is left; 'on' places it after the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded ribbon used as tape for waistbands and hats.
